grammar.Description: Chinese content questions use the same word order as statements; the question word appears where the answer would appear.
grammar.Example: 在中国的时候，你最喜欢吃的食物是什么？
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Zài Zhōngguó de shíhòu, nǐ zuì xǐhuan chī de shíwù shì shénme?

grammar.Description: For action sentences, time, people, preposition/place, and action follow a predictable order.
grammar.Example: 下个星期我们要去中国旅行。
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Xià ge xīngqī wǒmen yào qù Zhōngguó lǚxíng.

grammar.GrammarPoint: If A describes B, A comes before B
grammar.ShuoshuoStructureName: If A describes B, A comes before B
grammar.Description: Modifiers come before the noun or element they describe.
grammar.Example: 他是一个从来不说对不起的人。
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Tā shì yí ge cónglái bù shuō duìbuqǐ de rén.

grammar.Description: 和 can function as a preposition when there is mutual influence or relation.
grammar.Example: 最近我不可以和朋友见面。
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Zuìjìn wǒ bù kěyǐ hé péngyou jiànmiàn.
Wǒ zài Zhōngguó zhù le bā nián.

grammar.Description: 了 can mark change of state, completion, or appear in fixed phrases.
过 follows the verb and marks prior experience.
grammar.Example: 我从来没有想过这个问题。
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Wǒ cónglái méiyǒu xiǎng guo zhè ge wèntí.

grammar.Description: 给 can mean to/for and can introduce an indirect object or beneficiary.
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Wǒ gěi tā mǎi le yí ge lǐwù.

grammar.GrammarPoint: 有点儿 vs 一点儿
grammar.ShuoshuoStructureName: 有点儿 vs 一点儿
grammar.Description: 有点儿 often describes a slightly negative degree; 一点儿 often means a small amount or a bit more.
让 can mean let, make, or ask someone to do something.
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Tā bú ràng wǒ gàosu nǐ.

grammar.Description: 比 compares two things; negative comparison usually uses 没有.
grammar.Example: 他的车比我的贵一点儿。
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Tā de chē bǐ wǒ de guì yìdiǎnr.

grammar.Description: Question words with 都/也 can mean any/every/no depending on polarity and context.
grammar.Example: 我想去旅行，去哪里都可以。
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù lǚxíng, qù nǎli dōu kěyǐ.

grammar.Description: A resultative complement follows a verb directly and shows the result of the action.
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Zhè ge zì nǐ xiě cuò le.

grammar.Description: 的 modifies nouns, 地 modifies verbs, and 得 introduces degree/result comments after verbs or adjectives.
着 can mark a continuing state, location existence, manner of accompanying action, or repeated process leading to a result.
grammar.Example: 他穿着一件黑色的衣服。
grammar.ExamplePinyin: Tā chuān zhe yí jiàn hēisè de yīfu.
Wǒ bǎ shū huán gěi tā le.
Dàngāo bèi tā chī wán le.
